name: Alabama
agency: Alabama Law Enforcement Agency (ALEA), Driver License Division
permitAge: 15 (Stage I learner license; valid 4 years, renewable once)

teen.supervisedHours: Unresolved: ALEA GDL page says 50 hours behind-the-wheel (verification form signed by parent/guardian/instructor); ALEA form DL-31 and ADPH poster say 30 hours, with driver education as an alternative. Check statute 32-6-7.2.
teen.nightLimit: Stage II: no driving midnight-6 a.m. unless with parent, guardian, or licensed driver 21+; exceptions for work, school-sponsored and religious events, emergencies, hunting/fishing
teen.passengerLimit: Stage II: no more than one passenger besides parents, legal guardians or family members
teen.phone: Stage II: no handheld communication devices. All drivers: hands-free law since June 15, 2023 (no holding a device; secondary enforcement per news reports); texting ban since 2012 (32-5A-350)

notes: Stage III (unrestricted) at 17 after 6 months on Stage II; GDL violations extend restrictions 6 months or to age 18
Speed (32-5A-171 / ALEA): urban district 30 mph; interstate 70; other 4+ lane highways 65; other highways 55; county paved roads 45; unpaved roads 35
Left-lane law (32-5A-80, Act 2019-515): may not stay in the far-left lane of an interstate more than 1.5 miles without completely passing
Move Over Act: leave lane next to stopped emergency/tow/utility/garbage/road-work vehicle with flashing lights; if not possible slow to 15 mph under a limit of 25+ (10 mph under if limit 20 or less)
School bus: on a divided highway of 4+ lanes with a median only same-direction traffic stops; 4-lane road without median or with only a turn lane: both directions stop
Right turn on red allowed after a full stop unless a sign prohibits it (secondary sources)
Headlights required when wipers are in use for rain, sleet or snow (32-5-29, per Florence PD notice)
Knowledge test offered in Spanish and other languages (ALEA manual); question count/pass mark only from third-party sites (30 questions / 24 correct) - not confirmed officially
